speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: Mr Chairman, I beg to move, "That the total sum allocated for Head W of the Estimates be reduced by S$100".

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: Mr Chairman, in my kick-off speech for the Committee of Supply Debate for MOT, I would like to address two key developments in our transportation industry in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: The first, a recent unanticipated development – the first, a recent unanticipated development, the COVID-19 outbreak and its effect on the industry; and the second, MOT's strategic long-term plan for our rail network.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: As we know, Singapore has been under the cloud of the COVID-19 outbreak since the end of last year.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: We have been working extremely hard collectively to battle against the spread of the virus in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: Our healthcare team rightfully deserves our admiration and gratitude for their efforts on the frontline, looking after patients who have fallen ill because of the virus.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: However, Sir, there is also another team that has been on the frontline, bravely continuing to provide essential services to Singaporeans amid the ongoing virus outbreak.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: I am referring to our public transport team.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: I joined Senior Minister of State Janil Puthucheary and NTWU Executive Secretary Brother Melvin Yong last month to visit the Bedok Integrated Transport Hub and Tanah Merah MRT Station and we observed our public transport team doing their part to step up cleaning routines which are over and above their usual duties.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: They work very hard every day, putting themselves on the line in the fight against the virus outbreak so as to ensure that precautionary measures are taken to protect Singaporeans on our public transport network.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: I wish to take this opportunity to salute them for their efforts!

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: We also know that the virus outbreak has adversely affected the entire transportation industry.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: Travel numbers are down, whether in the air, on water or land.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: Transport operators and workers are concerned not only about bottom lines but also their own health as they go about their daily work.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: I am therefore extremely glad to see the various measures that the Government has put in place to support the transportation industry.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: Both taxi and private hire car operators have also set up temperature screening protocols for their drivers.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: Various other measures to support our aviation and marine transportation sectors were also announced at the Budget Statement earlier by Deputy Prime Minister Heng.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: These measures will go some way in alleviating the hardships and difficulties that the transportation industry is facing as a result of the virus outbreak.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: However, while we all hope that the virus outbreak can be contained quickly, in the past few weeks, we see worrying signs of further outbreaks in Japan, South Korea, Iran and Italy.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: If this continues, or worse if more countries get affected, it will inevitably have a further adverse effect on Singapore’s globally inter-connected economy.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: We must therefore confront the possibility that the worldwide spread of the COVID-19 virus could continue for some time to come and further affect our transportation industry.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: In the premises, I would like to invite the Minister to share with us further plans or measures that MOT could implement to support the transportation industry, in the event that the situation is drawn out over a prolonged period of time.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: On this front, we have much better news to share.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: As we are all aware, the Government has made and are still making significant investments to our rail network.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: The rapid expansion of our rail network continues over the next two decades.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: Announced projects include the Thomson-East Coast Line, Jurong Region Line, Circle Line extension and the Cross Island Line.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: Our extensive efforts to renew, expand and improve our rail network has clearly paid off!

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: I remember Minister Khaw, in 2017, setting a target of 1 million Mean Km Between Failure (MBKF) by 2020.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: This means that our trains, on average will travel about 1 million km before a delay of more than five minutes is recorded.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: We achieved this ambitious target by August 2019!

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: We will recollect that as recently as 2015, our rail reliability was at 133,000 MBKF, at about one-tenth of current reliability levels.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: In 2017, this number had increased to about 400,000 MBKF and finally, to current levels of above 1 million MBKF.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: The renewal of our rail network has led to higher reliability and shorter waiting times.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: The expansion of the rail network will lead to better accessibility, more convenience and comfort for commuters in the future.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: These are all positives and MOT should be lauded for achieving and indeed, surpassing, the herculean targets and tasks set.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: Investments made in the renewal and expansion of our rail network need to be funded.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Mr Chairman, the aviation sector has been adversely affected by COVID-19.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Many airlines and their crews are feeling the brunt because many flights have been cancelled and the passenger numbers for other flights have been reduced.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I have been to the airport several times over the last two or three weeks.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The situation is very tough – very few passengers.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Consequently, even taxi drivers share with me that they wait for about three hours for passengers.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: That has never happened before in the past.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: The Government announced a slew of packages involving training and support assistance.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Has it cushioned the impact and whether measures such as sending workers for upskilling have been implemented and well-subscribed?

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I know we are asking for some things to be sped up in the midst of these recent announcements, but indeed, the income and the flight hours have been shortened tremendously; and the help needs to be very imminent and fast.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Both local and foreign crew also operate as effective teams.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: We do not just need the Singapore crew.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: A lot of times, we need our foreign workers and our partners who fly and service the planes, and do all the necessary work at the airport.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: It is indeed critical that we retain and ready the core team for the upturn, following COVID-19.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Are there concerns among workers in the sector that remain unresolved and what more can we do to cushion and mitigate the impact?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: Chairman, I would like to declare my interest as the CEO of ComfortDelGro Taxi Business.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: COVID-19 hit Singapore suddenly and spread quite rapidly.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: We appreciate MOT's swift actions to announce plan to help our P2P drivers even before Budget day.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: By doing so, taxi operators are in the red but taxi drivers and P2P drivers are still suffering.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: Many P2P drivers met me at the coffeeshops, in the course of my work, to appeal to the Government to increase the quantum of SRF.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: Alternatively, LTA can help to provide tax rebates to P2P operators so that the operators can pass the savings to the P2P drivers.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: The Minister has openly said, many times, that the Government is willing to provide more help, as and when it is needed.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Some taxi drivers have shared with me that the assistance is not sufficient as the drop in their earnings have been substantial.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Changes in ridership patterns could also be longer term in nature.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: What are the training packages available to help drivers move on into other sectors?

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: I have been approached by a number of elderly residents who hold Taxi Driver's Vocational Licence (TDVL), highlighting the following two matters and requested that this be brought to Ministry's attention.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: First, the issue on the mandatory medical examination or health check-ups.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: It is a requirement for Qualified Driving Licence (QDL) holders aged 65 and above to go for health check once every three years for them to be allowed to continue driving.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: I also understand that for TDVL holders of the same age group, they are required to have their health checked on yearly basis.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Based on these two requirements, an individual age 65 years old and above has to attend medical examination once every three years.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: First, they have to fork out additional amount of money for their health check, and second, it affects their income since they have to sacrifice their driving hours to attend this medical examination.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: I do hope the Ministry will consider to allow elderly TDVL holders to undergo a single comprehensive medical examination, instead of two separate sessions, as mentioned earlier.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Second is the issue on the statutory age limit for vocational licence.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Currently, the statutory age limit for vocational licence is 75 years old.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: This extension will allow elderly TDVL holders who still need to sustain themselves to continue driving for few more years.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: And for those who just want to earn some income or remain active, they can do a part-time or relief driving.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Hope Ministry will look into the matters raised.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Png Eng Huat, you can take both your cuts together.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: In particular, I have called for the discretionary right turn junction to be phased out.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: If one were to Google the term "discretionary right turn", a list of accidents will pop up on the screen.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: There is even a petition asking LTA to ban such junctions all together.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: LTA was reported to have taken steps to address the safety concern of pedestrians over the years.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: I have noticed that more traffic light junctions are being re-programmed.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: I spoke on the same subject time and again, because I strongly believe those horrible accidents that happened at such junction could be avoidable.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: How is that not dangerous to begin with?

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: Imagine pedestrians and drivers hesitating at the discretionary right turn junction, second-guessing whether it is safe to proceed even though the lights are both in their favour.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: If a pedestrian could be assigned 15% blame in an accident, even though the lights were in his favour in the court of law, what is the proportion of blame for the Ministry for giving pedestrians a false sense of security a discretionary right turn, when the Green Man signal does not necessarily mean it is safe to cross any more?

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: I am not asking the Ministry to design a perfect traffic junction.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: I am asking the Ministry to take the guess work out of crossing a simple junction.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: Anything else, the pedestrians and motorists will have to take responsibility for.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: And if we are talking about cultivating patience on the road, would a split traffic junction not been ideal training ground for that?

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: Many Singaporeans welcome the idea of having lifts retrofitted to POBs, especially the elderly people with mobility issues, couples with baby on pram and anyone who finds climbing overhead bridges a challenge.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: I have written on behalf of many residents request for lifts for the overhead bridge in Hougang, in particular, the one at Holy Innocence High along Upper Serangoon Road.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: LTA has patiently replied to those residents, sharing about the high cost of retrofitting lifts to POBs and the priority being given to overhead bridges within 400 metres from polyclinics and hospitals.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: Retrofitting lifts to POBs is a challenging process in itself.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: Plots of land on both sides of the road would have to be acquired to make way for the lift shafts.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: The construction along the narrow stretch of the foot path is challenging and the whole process may take quite a while to complete.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: The lifts at the overhead bridge along Hougang Avenue 2 have been under construction for almost two years and they are still not ready.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: But having lift access for all which may not be an ideal solution for an ageing society like ours.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: If the lifts were to break down or to undergo servicing, everything would be reverted to leg power again.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: The rationale of having POBs to serve a car-lite and ageing society may need a rethink.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: I hope the Ministry can study into the possibility of converting those heavily used POBs in HDB heartlands to signalise pedestrian crossings.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: This will allow pedestrians with mobility issues or special needs to cross the road, come what may, even if the traffic lights are out of order.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: Maybe the Ministry can share what is the cost of implementing and maintaining a signalised pedestrian crossing versus retrofitting an existing overhead bridge with lifts.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: The issue of having too many signalised pedestrian crossings along a stretch of the road, can be easily overcome with synchronised traffic light control.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: And if we are talking about a pedestrian-centric and car-lite city, getting drivers to exercise a little patience would fit the overall objective quite nicely.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: While the fare formula has added the network capacity factor to address rising operating cost deficits, cost management is also important.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Could the Ministry update us on efforts to optimise public transport services to manage costs?

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Some commuters will also be affected when service frequency and availability is optimised.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: This makes it hard for the public and hon Members to support cost management.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Could we consider "win-win" solutions where we issue targeted, transitional public transport vouchers to commuters who have to bear the brunt of any service changes?

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: As such, I would like MOT to give an update of the measures that we are taking to stay ahead of the pack and how we are also preparing our workforce in the air and maritime transport industry to keep up with the changes ahead.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Dennis Tan, you may take your three cuts.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I declare my interest as a member of the shipping community in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Last month, I filed a Parliamentary Question (PQ) asking (a) whether any investigation is being carried out in respect to the piracy incidents in the Singapore Strait in and after December 2019; (b) has the Government identified the persons or groups responsible for the reported incidents and where they originated from; (c) what action has been taken by any of our Government agencies to date; and (d) what are the Government's plans to prevent similar acts of piracy?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: He said that as the Singapore Strait does not only include Singapore territorial waters, the fight against piracy requires collaboration among all partners.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: On a same sitting in February two hon Members in this House also filed questions relating to the piracy incidents to the Minister for Defence.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Minister Ng Eng Hen in his reply to one Member talked about RSN's cooperation with neighbouring counterparts under the MSP.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I had filed the PQ to the Minister for Transport instead of the Minister for Defence, as MOT is the domain Ministry for maritime transport, and in my view, this goes beyond the issue of security or security arrangements with our neighbouring countries.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Minister Ng's answer also shed no light on the same.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The port of Singapore is one of the busiest ports in the world.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Many ships pass through the Strait of Singapore every day for which a large number comes through to the port of Singapore and is anchorages and even its Outside Port Limits (OPL) waters for a variety of commercial shipping, bunkering and ancillary activities.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: It does not matter to shipowners or uses that the Straits of Singapore is not entirely subsumed under our territorial waters.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Many shipowners and users associate the Strait of Singapore with the access and passage between the Malacca Strait and the South China Sea and with access to the Port of Singapore and its OPL.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: It is therefore in the interest of MOT, MPA and indeed all stakeholders in the Port of Singapore and our maritime hub, that the Strait of Singapore and its adjacent waters are kept safe and free of piracy activities.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: In fact, in my view, it is in the greater interest of Singapore, as compared to our neighbours, that piracy activities are minimised or curbed.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: We have seen from the piracy problems off the coast of Somalia and the Gulf of Aden, not so long ago, and more recently off West Africa, how piracy result in increase in insurance and other operating costs for shipowners and operators, and shipping costs for shippers.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Well, the piracy situation in the Strait of Singapore and the Strait of Malacca is thankfully far better than what we have seen in the waters off Somalia or West Africa.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This is something we should not take for granted.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: In July last year, the Chinese government raised the security level on Chinese flagged ships transiting the Strait of Malacca.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I hope MOT and other Singapore Government agencies involved will work actively with our counterparts in neighbouring countries to (a) understand the causes of all piracy incidents regardless of the locality of each incident; and (b) help bring all culprits to justice or encourage neighbouring authorities to work towards that end.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: By doing the above, I hope all parties and all countries can work to minimise or curb piracy activities in the region.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: But Senior Minister of State said that MOT will only be touching on the extended cycling power network during the COS debate today.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Direct access to the extended cycling lane network cannot be a half-hearted attempt, for example, having cycling paths circling a number of HDB blocks, but with no direct link from each block; or having cycling paths circling around clusters of private residential estates, expecting e-scooter or other users to alight and push en route to cycling paths.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Similarly, people going to work in office buildings or industrial estates, must have direct access without having to travel on surfaces on which their mode of devices are barred.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: In fact, going one step further towards utopia, if our cycling path network were to become sufficiently extensive such that PMD riders do not need to alight and push.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: It may in turn do away with the need for cyclists to share the use of foot path, which is still currently allowed.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: And this prospect will be welcomed by many footpath users who may not think that sharing footpaths with cyclists is a safe idea at all.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: It is not a safe idea because we still have a riding culture problem.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: If there is no direct link between the extended cycling network and the homes or workplaces of Singaporeans, e-scooter users would technically have to alight and push their e-scooters when on roads or footpaths and e-bike users must push their e-bikes when passing through footpaths.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: How confident are we that all riders will comply accordingly?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The new cycling lanes with a more extensive network alone will not solve all the problems we have seen with e-scooters before the footpath ban.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Most of these problems, I submit, had to do with a poor riding culture, inadequate public education and inadequate enforcement.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: With the new mandatory competency test certification for all users, I hope the public education situation with riders will improve considerably.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: However, for the non-riding public, I hope the Government will take steps and review how it can improve its public education.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The Government must think of how to push such information to people who do not seek it, and such efforts should be carried out in all our four official languages.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: On the issue of enforcement, people may take their chances and continue to use their devices illegally or in unlawful ways if they think that the chances of meeting enforcement officers are slim.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Even now, I still see e-scooters being ridden on the road or on footpaths, albeit in a limited way.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I still see illegal specs e-bikes being used and e-bikes on footpaths.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I have also in the past suggested that the Government should consider mandatory safe riding certification courses with disqualification rights.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The competency test certification process adopted last month is a big step forward.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I believe that with disqualification rights, people will take greater care to use their e-scooters safely and considerately.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: So, I would again urge MOT to incorporate disqualification rights in our law.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The new Acts do not provide details on this.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: It is important to ensure all food delivery companies will take ownership of the issue of their riders using lawful devices or riding lawfully and safely during their deliveries.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: On the very day the Government banned e-scooters from footpaths, Deliveroo announced that they would stop working with e-scooter delivery riders on footpaths.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: However, I continue to see GrabFood delivery riders using e-scooters on footpaths or roads even in the last two weeks.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I am shocked that GrabFood still allow their delivery riders to carry out delivery in an unlawful manner and I hope that MOT will take action.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: For example, PMDs being used on the road, rider using an illegal specs e-scooter or PAB rider using footpaths.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I am concerned that if allowed, claims by injured parties may be frustrated when accidents take place in such scenarios, which may defeat the very purpose of requiring such insurance coverage, particularly when the rider is self-employed and own his own device.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: While we have always mentioned that cycling is a good mode of transport for first and last mile connectivity and the focus has been to increase intra-town cycling network, can I also suggest that the MOT look at the possibility of cycling being a viable mode of transport for the entire journey?

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Singapore is a small island and cycling is a good form of exercise.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: For someone working within 10 km of their workplace, cycling could be a good alternative if there are good inter-town cycling paths.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: My hope is that it would be possible for my residents to cycle from Jurong West to Raffles Place on designated cycling paths in the future.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Ang Wei Neng, you can take both your cuts.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: Does it mean that we are really trying to accelerate?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: We hope that MOT will give a firmer update on the timeline?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: Does it mean that we are aiming to build 1,300 km of cycling paths five years earlier, that means by 2025?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: In determining exactly how the cycling paths should be laid out, to what extent does MOT consult with the local community?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: For instance, as cycling paths are typically carved out of existing footpaths for the more mature estates, who decides if the cycling paths are to be located on the left or right of the footpaths?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: Who decides the footpath were to be sandwiched between the cycling path and the road or the cycling path be sandwiched between the footpath and the road?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: Also, from past experiences, we encounter problems with mature trees blocking the potential new cycling path or shared path.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: How is MOT coordinating with the various Ministries to expedite the construction of these cycling paths?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: Chairman, my next cut is on Operating Train Services Overseas.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: This morning, there is a breakdown in the train service from Bishan to Yio Chu Kang, so that prompted me to change my speech.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: Singapore's train system has surpassed 1 million train-km between delays of more than five minutes.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: I do not know whether this morning's breakdown, how will it affect the 1 million mark.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: However, nothing is perfect, just like when Police say Singapore has low crime, it does not mean there is no crime.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: When Singapore Airport is ranked the best airport in the world for a few years, it does not mean there is no lost luggage in Changi Airport.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: Likewise, it is unreasonable to expect the train system be perfect and no breakdown at all.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: It is more important to build resilience within the train system; and the Circle Line and Downtown line have added resilience and some redundancy with the train system.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: Similarly, the upcoming Thomson Eastern Line as well as Cross Island Line will build more resilience within the system.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: So, train passengers then can have alternatives when one line is down – like the London train system.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: By operating train services overseas, it will enable us to learn the best practices first hand and also bring the best to Singapore.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: Train operators like Hong Kong's MTR has been operating overseas for quite some time.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: They have been operating 1,000 km of track in London, Stockholm and Australia.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: Similarly, French state-owned public transport company RATP operates in 14 countries and they have deep knowledge in how to operate the train system.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
text: At some point of time, I would like to ask the Minister when will the Singapore fraternity, the train fraternity, consider operating the train system overseas, share our expertise overseas and bring the best to Singapore?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: Indeed, both LRT lines were upgraded to two-car operations in 2016 and load on the systems would surely have increased.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: SPLRT did see some preventive maintenance and asset renewal works between 2017 and 2018.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: However, if past experience with the MRT system is any indication, should we expect that more works ought to be done to maintain and improve on the reliability numbers of the LRT system?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Mr Chairman, I am heartened to see that the efforts of our extensive multi-year, multi-billion dollars rail renewal projects are now bearing fruit.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: But as we applaud the good work done thus far, we must not become complacent, or else, we risk undoing all that we have managed to achieve thus far.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I would also like to ask if the Ministry has any plans to renew and refurbish our older MRT stations, in particular, along the North-South and East-West Lines, some of which were built more than 33 years ago.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Rail maintenance workers are our unsung heroes in Singapore’s journey towards better rail reliability.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: They have been working hard day and night, including on weekends and public holidays, to carry out both maintenance and renewal works.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Some have raised issues regarding the lack of sufficient lighting and ventilation when carrying out their work in the MRT tunnels.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: With an increasing network of tracks underground, it is important that we take care of the welfare of our workers.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I have been into the tunnels on several occasions to observe track renewal as well as tunnel cleaning work.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Rail maintenance is back-breaking work, and I hope that the Ministry can look at improving the work conditions for our rail workers.

speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
text: Chairman, I would like to declare my interest as the General Secretary of Singapore Port Workers Union.

speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
text: The development of Tuas South is picking up pace.

speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
text: Sembcorp Marine shifted its HQ to Tuas in 2019, bringing along a large number of its workforce from other parts of Singapore office as they consolidated operations in Tuas.

speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
text: While the initial workforce numbers remain small, it will grow over time as more container berths become operational over the coming years.

speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
text: In my engagement with workers and union leaders, one of the main concerns was the distance between home and work.

speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
text: Based on SMRT's website, a commuter will take around 90 minutes to commute between Pasir Ris and Tuas Link, and approximately 72 minutes he stays up-north from Yishun to Tuas Link.

speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
text: Together with the sectoral tripartite partners, interim transport solutions have been put in place to cater to the workers' travelling needs.

speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
text: It is just a temporary solution and not a permanent solution.

speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
text: Can MOT reconsider the proposal for an automated people mover system in light of workforce growth in Tuas South?

speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
text: Can the Minister also share what would the projected ridership numbers be for Tuas South in five and 10 years' time?

speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
text: What are the long-term transport plans for Tuas South and how does MOT intend to address workers' concern on reducing their commuting time, especially for those staying in the eastern part of Singapore?

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Most commuters who take the MRT will notice that there have been marked improvements in train capacity, train reliability and comfort.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: As a regular MRT commuter, let me thank the Transport Minister and the team at MOT and all the people who have helped make improvements to the rail network system.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: As we continue to push for a car-lite society, may I urge MOT to consider having more public bus services to shuttle private estate residents to and from their homes to MRT stations during peak hours.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Currently, whenever I request for a bus service, the usual response from LTA is that there are adequate options.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: But if adequate options means to walk a distance in the hot sun or rainy weather to the bus stop, then most residents will stick to driving their cars to their office.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Hence, I urge MOT to make an extra effort to make public transport more convenient for residents.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Offer them a shuttle bus service to bring them to the nearest MRT station.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: If that extra effort is not made, it is unlikely that we will be able to persuade the residents to give up the comfort and convenience of their cars to walk a longer distance in the hot sun or rainy weather, just to take public transport.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Make it so convenient that it is a no-brainer to take public transport as compared to their private cars.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Next, may I ask Minister for an update as to the completion date for the eastern sector of the Thomson East Coast Line (TEL).

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: I have four stations in my constituency and many of my residents are very excited about having a new train line near their homes.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: These highly threatened monkeys are only found in the Central Catchment Nature Reserve.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: While mitigation measures have been proposed, Dr Andie feels that these measures will not work.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: She personally told me that she fears for the survival of this species.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: MOT has successfully achieved bold target of 1 million km between failure, as set by Minister Khaw in 2017.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: Our trains are now as reliable as the Taipei Metro and Hong Kong MTR.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: I applaud the team for their resilience, determination and hard work in achieving the target.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: Beyond ensuring timely renewal and maintenance of assets, we also need to build a pool of ever ready and competent rail engineering and maintenance crew to cope with a rapidly expanding rail network.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: Can the Minister share details of the training and upskilling programmes available for rail engineers?

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: How have these programmes led to the recent improvement in rail reliability and whether these programmes would be further enhanced?

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Melvin Yong, you can take your three cuts together.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Chairman, our rail network will grow significantly over this new decade.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The addition of three new lines – the Thomson-East Coast Line, Jurong Region Line and Cross Island Line – will increase the length of our rail network by about 130 km, bringing the total network length to about 360 km in 2030.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: As our rail industry grow, we need to upskill existing workers and recruit more rail professionals to run the expanded and more complex train network.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The $100 million Rail Manpower Development Package, announced by Minister in November 2019, will help accelerate this transformation of our rail workforce.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Can the Ministry provide an update on the initiatives under the Rail Manpower Development Package?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Additionally, how many workers are expected to benefit from these initiatives?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Chairman, my next cut will focus on the future of our land transport system, which will be electric, connected and autonomous.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: First, I applaud the Government for its ambition to phase out Internal Combustion Engine vehicles by 2040 and to embrace Electric Vehicles (EVs).

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Can the Ministry provide an update on the growth of EVs in Singapore over the past five years?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Fleet vehicles, such as our public buses, will be key in driving critical mass for islandwide EV-adoption.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Does the Ministry have plans to replace all public buses with electric buses and what will be the timeline?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Will our island's charging infrastructure be sufficient for the mass adoption of EVs?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Could the Ministry provide an update on the various Autonomous Vehicle trials and whether the plan to pilot autonomous buses in Punggol, Tengah and the Jurong Innovation District in the early 2020s is still on track?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Chairman, my final cut will be on the Bus Contracting Model (BCM).

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The introduction of BCM in 2016 has indeed transformed our public bus industry to become more competitive.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Today, we have four public bus operators operating 14 bus packages.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Commuters are enjoying better service reliability and reduced wait times, resulting in bus ridership hitting an all-time high of over four million daily rides in 2018.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: But as I highlighted in last year's Committee of Supply debate, BCM is not without its drawbacks.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Bus captains have informed me that their jobs today, are now more stressful than ever, as they have to meet new stringent KPIs imposed.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Could the Ministry share how it intends to mitigate this additional stress faced by our frontline bus captains?

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Additionally, I would like to ask if the Ministry has learnt any lessons from the tendering of the first four BCM packages and if there will be any changes to the future tenders.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Lastly, I would like for the Ministry to update on their plans to enhance our public bus infrastructure to keep up with the increase in our public bus fleets and to cater for the introduction of electric buses.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: Before I proceed, I will like to declare my interest as the CEO of ComfortDelGro Taxi business.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: I have explicitly supported the plan to roll out more clean and green vehicles last week in the Parliament.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: However, I will like to make a few clarifications today.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: What kind of incentives will Government provide for real estate owners, car park owners or operators or new players to install more new charging points?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: Come 2030, how many EVs can be supported by 28,000 charging points?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: If most of the EVs are charging at about the same time, say in the evening, do we need to upgrade our Power Grid?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: In short, EEAI alone is not as attractive as VES.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: Does MOT have plan to continue with VES next year so as to supplement and compliment the EEAI?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: We will like to seek clarity so that fleet owners can better support Government's green initiative.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Chairman, one of the biggest challenges to EV ownership currently is the network of public EV Chargers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Other providers include Greenlots and some car dealers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Private property owners can install a wall box which are charging units, especially installed by the dealer at the electric vehicle owners' place of choice.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: However, the vast majority of consumers live in high-rise buildings.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Greenlots, for instance, is installing charging stations at a small number of Condominiums and requires MCST approvals to do so.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: What potentially are some of the bottlenecks and what is the plan contingent on?

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: How does the Ministry envision building charging points in public places and for private property owners?

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
text: The project benefits both countries by easing causeway congestion, reducing travelling time and facilitating business and tourism.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
text: On 4 November 2019, it was announced that a suspension of the RTS project will be extended until 30 April 2020.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
text: With a new government in Malaysia and the April deadline approaching, can the Minister provide an update on our bilateral transport projects.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
text: If there is no progress, what other options are there to improve connectivity between the two countries and improving the Customs, Immigration and Quarantine (CIQ) facilities at our border.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Mr Chairman, COVID-19 is still wreaking havoc around the world.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: In Singapore, Changi Airport took the first hit.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Both the cruise and ferry sectors are devastated.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: As China locks down, global supply chains are also disrupted.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: As fear grips, people telecommute more and go out less.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: This has taken a toll on the livelihoods of our taxi and private hire car drivers.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: We are also tracking the impact on our transport infrastructure projects.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: For now, the delay to project timelines is still manageable.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: But if the outbreak drags on, it could disrupt the supply of construction equipment and materials.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: This could impact the timeline for Terminal 5, Tuas Port, new MRT stations and the next-generation ERP system.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: For example, our new trains are being built in China.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: With support from our tripartite partners, the Government reacted swiftly with a robust Unity Budget 2020.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: For the transport sector, MOT worked closely with NTUC and our transport operators to put in place relief measures to support our workers, while providing assurance to our commuters.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Sooner or later, our economy and our industries will recover.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: While we attend to the immediate needs, we should also focus on the eventual recovery and make full use of this lull period.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: First, position our companies and workers to ride the eventual upturn.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: We have the road maps, the air, land and sea transport Industry Transformation Maps, to show us the way forward.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Over the next five years, we have an extensive line-up of construction projects in the transport sector.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: On the aviation front, we are expanding Changi Airport.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: The third runway will be operational by the middle of 2020s.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: The development of Terminal 5 is well underway.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: On the maritime front, Tuas Port Phase 1 will be fully operational by 2027.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: When fully completed in the 2040s, Tuas Port will be the world’s single largest fully-automated container terminal.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Together, these investments will grow our external connectivity to seize growth in the global transport of goods and people.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Another international link is the proposed RTS Link with Malaysia.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Miss Cheng Li Hui asked about the progress.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Recent political developments in Malaysia will further impact the project.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: While we remain committed to working with Malaysia to find a way forward, the project cannot be suspended indefinitely.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: We, therefore, look forward to hearing from Malaysia soon.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Are there other options to address the Causeway jam?

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Expanding the immigration facilities will help as the current capacity is inadequate to handle the peak traffic.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Better distribution of traffic between the Causeway and the Second Link will also help.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Likewise, a better distribution of traffic between peak and off-peak periods.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: We have been trying to pursue all these options, but to move the needle meaningfully, the RTS Link is the answer.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: But beyond the immediate, our vision is a clean and green transport system for Singapore.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: This will raise the quality of life for generations of Singaporeans to come.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: First, phase out vehicles with internal combustion engines (ICE) by 2040.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: In other words, no more ICE vehicles by 2040!

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: We have 20 years to phase them out.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Senior Minister of State Dr Janil Puthucheary will explain how we can achieve this and replace them with cleaner vehicles.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Second, speed up the construction of our cycling infrastructure.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Senior Minister of State Dr Lam Pin Min will explain how we can get more Singaporeans to Walk-Cycle-Ride for first-mile and last-mile connectivity.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Third, keep our public transport among the best in the world.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: As noted by Mr Ang Wei Neng, Mr Sitoh Yih Pin, Miss Cheng Li Hui, Mr Melvin Yong and Mr Lim Biow Chuan, we have turned the corner on rail reliability.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: So, let me join these Members to thank our transport workers – LTA, SMRT, SBST and the National Transport Workers’ Union – for their hard work and dedication.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: But remember, a highly reliable MRT line may still experience some occasional hiccups.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: We do our best to reduce such inconveniences to the absolute minimum.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: I note Mr Ang Wei Neng’s suggestion that our rail operators should seek to venture abroad, as our bus operators have done.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: This is something for the operators to decide.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: But if they do, my advice is that their foreign ventures should not distract them from their domestic operations in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Their priority must always be to ensure safe, smooth and reliable journeys for our commuters in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: In any case, our two rail operators will be fully engaged with our domestic network.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: There is plenty of work to be done.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Over the next decade, we will be spending over $60 billion to expand and renew our rail network – $60,000 million of works to be done.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: First, we will be completing the Thomson-East Coast Line (TEL).

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Stage 2 will follow within the next few months – single digit months.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Mr Lim Biow Chuan and his residents in Mountbatten will benefit from Stage 4 of TEL by 2023.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Can we expedite further? "Jing kang kor" – I think very difficult.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Every time I meet the team, my message to them is "safety first".

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Certainly, you want it done as soon as possible.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: We will see four new stations added to our rail network.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: This includes the opening of Hume Station by 2025, which Mayor Low Yen Ling has actively lobbied for in previous COS.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: This year, I did not find her "cut".

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Third, we will be completing the Circle Line when we complete the circle.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Fourth, we will be completing the Jurong Region Line by 2028.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Like Mr Arasu Duraisamy, we want our Tuas port workers to have good public transport to Tuas.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: This is in addition to the Tuas West Extension and bus services 247 and 248 in the Tuas South area which we had put in over the past few years.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: In fact, a Singaporean student studying in Geneva, Faiz Basha, was so excited by the plan for our rail network that he produced a revised MRT map for 2030 and beyond.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Mr Cedric Foo referred me to this map.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: He was intrigued by it and he described it as a beautiful map and, indeed, it is.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Senior Minister of State Dr Janil Puthucheary told me of another Singaporean, architect Cliff Tan, based in the UK who has offered LTA many similar design suggestions.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Both are overseas but their hearts are firmly anchored in Singapore!

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: We would have achieved or exceeded the level of train connectivity enjoyed by the residents in Hong Kong, Tokyo and New York today.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: This year is 2020; so, in only two to three years' time, Mr Lim!

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: By then, we would also be able to see the benefits from the renewal of our oldest LRT line, the Bukit Panjang LRT.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Ageing train stations, too, will be suitably refurbished and upgraded, especially the toilets and escalators.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: In time, we will also need to renew the next oldest lines – North East Line and Sengkang Punggol LRT – in good time.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: The hard lesson learnt from the problems earlier faced by SMRT is that we must invest in good operations and maintenance.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: As noted by Miss Cheng Li Hui, this means engineering capabilities, as well as the timely renewal of old MRT and LRT lines.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: As we pursue these projects, let me assure Mr Melvin Yong that we will continue to work with operators and unions to ensure optimal working conditions for our transport workers.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Mr Yong knows that these are my top concerns.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Every time I visit a depot, I would check in, talk to them, take a good look at their lounge, the furniture, the toilets.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Those are signs whether the operators are paying attention.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: They form the backbone of our transport system.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: We must support them well so that they can perform to their maximum potential.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Mr Chairman, transport is both capital-intensive and skills-intensive.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: That is why MOT’s budget is among the biggest in the Government.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: I think we are at number four this year although, in terms of the number of "cuts", we are at the bottom four, I think.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: To ensure sustainability, we need taxpayers and commuters to co-fund it.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: The question is how to share the burden fairly.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: As posed by Mr Sitoh Yih Pin just now, it is how to strike a balance between financial sustainability, affordability, reliability and efficiency.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: It requires hard-headed calculations and a heavy dose of empathy.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: It requires political honesty and also sound judgement.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: That is why, among other things, we have a process comprising an objective fare formula and an independent Public Transport Council.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: I agree with Assoc Prof Walter Theseira that fare adjustments must be accompanied by serious cost containment.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: We will continue to look for cost-cutting measures and productivity improvement solutions.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: We will also regularly benchmark our operators’ costs with their counterparts elsewhere.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: A recent NTU study gave us some reassurance that our operators’ costs are well within normal range.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: But we must also have the discipline to deploy public transport services prudently.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: That is why we have to sometimes turn down Members’ requests for new bus services – shuttle service, maybe we can negotiate – or shorter headways.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: In the coming years, the expansion of rail and cycling lane infrastructure will add greater connectivity to the system and benefit more commuters.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: A highly interconnected transport network, supported by real-time information, will provide commuters with more route and mode options.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Good mobile apps will empower commuters to choose the option that best meets their needs.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: As travel patterns change, we must be nimble to optimise the provision of public transport services.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: One such considerate Member is Mr Lim Biow Chuan.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: I have heard his request for additional public bus service for his private estate residents.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: I live in a private estate where there is a shuttle bus going around.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: In fact, it was the first private estate shuttle that runs on electricity – electric bus.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Mr Chairman, over the years, we have progressively transformed our land transport sector to better serve Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: It has not been a smooth journey but we never let difficulties discourage us.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Mr Ang Wei Neng referred to McKinsey’s 2018 report ranking Singapore’s public transport as amongst the best in the world.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: More recently, there was a Business Insider France (11 February 2020) report on urban mobility, in which consulting firm Oliver Wyman joined forces with the Berkeley University of California to rank the top 10 advanced cities in the world based on the quality of their public transport systems.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Credit must go to successive generations of MOT and LTA officials who put their heart and soul into this venture.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: My other MOT colleagues will now elaborate on our other plans moving forward.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: Mr Chairman, Minister Khaw spoke about the impact of COVID-19 on our transport network and our strategies for eventual recovery.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: He also laid down the vision of a clean and green transport system in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: I will now elaborate on our efforts in the aviation and maritime sectors, and share how we can develop our cycling infrastructure to complement our vision for a clean and green transport network.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: COVID-19 has hurt the aviation and maritime sectors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: Passenger traffic at Changi Airport and cruise and ferry passenger numbers have declined significantly.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: Our priority for the coming months is clear: first, help industry tide over this difficult time; and second, position for recovery so that we emerge from this even stronger.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: First, we will help the aviation and maritime sectors tide over this difficult time.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: We will also provide targeted assistance to affected ferry operators and other enterprises located at Marina South Pier and West Coast Pier.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: We are also helping companies reduce their costs so that they can help Singaporeans keep their jobs and use this time to go for training.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: Take, for example, airline crew, which Mr Ang Hin Kee asked about.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: Notwithstanding this, SIA is committed to helping its crew keep their jobs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: The Government is supporting this, through rebates on landing and parking charges, waivers of regulatory fees and the Jobs Support Scheme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: These measures will help ease the financial pressure and support the retention of local employees.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: Early this week, SkillsFuture Singapore (SSG), Workforce Singapore (WSG), the Civil Aviation Authority of Singapore (CAAS) and NTUC announced an enhanced training funding and support package for air transport companies; we will work with airlines to facilitate their staff, including cabin crew, to attend training courses and will monitor the take-up rate.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: We are watching the situation very closely and stand ready to do more if the situation worsens.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: Our commitment to our aviation and maritime sectors is this: we will get through this together.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: Working together as SGUnited, we can overcome COVID-19.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: Second, we will work with industry to position for recovery so that we emerge from this even stronger.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: Mr Yee Chia Hsing asked how we can keep our air and sea hubs competitive.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: To stay competitive, we will invest in the three Cs – Capacity, Capability and Connectivity – and at the same time, develop sustainability as our new priority.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: Current challenges notwithstanding, air passenger numbers are expected to double from four billion to eight billion globally in the next 20 years; one in two of this growth, or 50% of this growth will be in Asia.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: For the maritime sector, the growth outlook is likewise positive.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: These translate to huge demand for capacity, capability and connectivity and offer tremendous opportunities for Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: First, on capacity, we will press on with the development of Changi Terminal 5 and Tuas Port so that we are in time with new infrastructural capacity to meet future demand.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: We are not done building our air and sea hubs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: Our efforts will not be hampered by COVID-19.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: We cannot meet the new demand just by growing manpower; we need to leverage technology and raise productivity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: We will help companies transform and capture new opportunities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: Since 2015, the Fund has already helped nearly 80 organisations raise productivity through over 200 initiatives.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: Real value-add per worker has increased by over 7% between 2015 and 2018.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: It uses augmented reality technology to track the real-time location of baggage and cargo units and helps workers cut loading time.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: The Maritime Port Authority of Singapore (MPA) and IMDA have also launched the Digital Acceleration Index to help maritime companies self-evaluate their digital maturity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: MPA and the Singapore Shipping Association will take this a step further to launch the Maritime Innovation Playbook to help companies develop their digitalisation plans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: Companies can also tap on MPA's Maritime Cluster Fund and the Sea Transport Industry Digitalisation Plan to support their digitalisation efforts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: We will also equip workers with new skills to take on new and better jobs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: We will train up a younger generation of Singaporeans so that they can benefit and grow with the air and sea industries.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: While demand may be down now, we will continue to maintain connectivity so that we can bounce back quickly when recovery returns.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: We will continue to push for air services liberalisation, to strengthen existing connections to cities and to build new ones.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: We will also go beyond physical connectivity to build digital connectivity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: MPA's digitalPORT@SG™ will streamline digital port clearance processes for ships calling at Singapore and improve the efficiency of vessel calls.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: Likewise, digitalOCEANS™ will link us up to other maritime-related digital platforms globally to improve efficiency in the global supply chain.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: The safety and security of our sea-lanes is fundamental to maritime connectivity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: Mr Dennis Tan asked what more we can do to address piracy and armed robbery incidents in the Strait of Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: The RSN's Maritime Security Task Force will also be enhancing their capabilities to deal with maritime threats.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: Other actions are also taken to combat piracy and armed-robbery.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: MPA advises commercial vessels to stay vigilant, keep a lookout for pirates and take anti-piracy measures, such as holding training drills.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: Singapore is also part of a region-wide initiative called ReCAAP (Regional Cooperation Agreement on Combating Piracy & Armed Robbery against ships in Asia), which facilitates timely and accurate information sharing so that the respective littoral States and the shipping community can take prompt remedial actions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: While we position ourselves to seize the growth opportunities in aviation and maritime, we will do so sustainably.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: Singapore will not just be a competitive international transport hub but also a sustainable one.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: On the aviation front, we will play our part to contribute towards the International Civil Aviation Organization’s (ICAO)'s aspirational goals of 2% annual fuel efficiency improvement and carbon neutral growth from 2020 onwards.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: Under the scheme, our airlines will freeze their carbon footprint at current levels by reducing emissions and purchasing carbon credits.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: Second, Singapore's aviation community will work together towards greener aviation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: Singapore Airlines has invested in the latest aircraft models that are more fuel efficient and has an average fleet age that is nearly half that of the industry.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: CAAS, our Air Navigation Service Provider, will continue to invest in new technologies and air traffic management processes to improve flow and cut delays.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: In 2019, these processes reduced about 130,000 tonnes of carbon emissions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: Changi Airport Group will continue to invest in environmental sustainability initiatives, such as energy-efficient cooling systems, infrastructure for charging electric vehicles and renewable energy options.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: Third, we will study the use of sustainable aviation fuels (SAFs) in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: SAFs can reduce emissions by up to 80% over their life cycle compared to conventional jet fuel, but they are two to five times more expensive today.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: Singapore houses key global aerospace companies and fuel producers, such as Rolls Royce, Shell and Neste.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: The Government and the industry players are studying different business and technological models to enable economically viable and sustainable SAF supply chains in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: On the maritime front, Singapore is committed to environmentally sustainable international shipping under the leadership of the International Maritime Organization (IMO).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: Beyond this, the IMO has set a longer term target to reduce the total annual greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions caused by international shipping by at least 50% by 2050, from 2008 levels.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: While IMO2050 is still 30 years away, we will start making plans now so that our companies and workers are equipped to seize new opportunities that arise from the shift.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: First, MPA will launch the Maritime Singapore Decarbonisation Blueprint 2050 next year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: The blueprint will chart out strategies to achieve a sustainable maritime Singapore and establish Singapore as a responsible hub port and international maritime centre.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: Second, the Singapore Maritime Foundation will set up an International Advisory Panel to garner inputs from local and international leaders from the industry and academia for this effort.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: Mr Chairman, this is what we do to help our aviation and maritime sectors compete, always looking beyond the horizon, planning for the long term, working in close partnership with workers and companies, and this will distinguish Singapore from other competing cities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: Our land transport system also plays an important role in securing a sustainable future for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: We will continue to work towards our car-lite vision and promote public, shared and active modes of transport as they are the most environmentally sustainable.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: I will touch on our efforts to promote active mobility, which has a low environmental footprint and complements our public transport system in moving towards a car-lite Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: In cultivating a sustainable active mobility landscape, we have enhanced our regulatory and enforcement regimes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: With the recent ban on e-scooters on footpaths and enhanced regulatory regime on active mobility devices, path safety has improved.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: As Mr Dennis Tan said, businesses have a role to play, which is why LTA has introduced regulations on companies and continues to work closely with companies to encourage responsible behaviour by their riders.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: One requirement is that companies must ensure that all riders they hire in the course of work have third party liability insurance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: LTA will specify minimum requirements for these insurance policies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: Mr Dennis Tan also pointed out the importance of public education and enforcement.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: That is why we are introducing a mandatory theory test for all e-scooter and power-assisted bicycle (PAB) riders to educate and raise awareness.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: We have also enhanced the penalties to strengthen deterrence against offences like speeding and reckless riding.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: LTA will not hesitate to take errant riders to task.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: Regarding Mr Dennis Tan's suggestion to disqualify riders who commit serious offences from riding, we will work with the Active Mobility Advisory Panel (AMAP) to study if it is necessary to do so, depending on the safety situation going forward.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: Several Members have asked about our infrastructure plans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: They will be pleased to know that we are accelerating the development of cycling paths.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: By 2023, all HDB towns will have cycling paths.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
