text: All HDB residents will have direct access to a wider cycling path network that is almost double the existing network.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: Residents can look forward to the cycling path plans for their towns within the year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: LTA is working closely with Government agencies and local communities to ensure that the cycling path network meets the needs of the residents.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: Towns which currently lack cycling paths or have many active mobility device users will have cycling paths built first.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: For towns with cycling path networks, we will continue to enhance connectivity, so that residents can enjoy more seamless access to key transport nodes and amenities like the town centre, MRT stations, eateries and malls.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: And as Mr Ang Wei Neng has highlighted, constructing cycling paths in mature towns require trade-offs, especially in densely built-up mature towns.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: In some cases, we may have no choice but to reclaim grass verges and affect trees.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: In others, we may need to re-purpose roads.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: With this, eight in 10 HDB residents will be a few minutes away from the cycling path network.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: Most HDB residents will be within 250 m from the nearest cycling path.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: This cycling path density is comparable to cities such as Amsterdam or Copenhagen.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: HDB Residents can expect to reach their nearest town centre within 20 minutes using active mobility modes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: Singaporeans will benefit from a comprehensive cycling path network connecting all HDB towns.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: The expanded cycling path network will allow more inter-town journeys to be carried out entirely on cycling paths.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: Active mobility device users can look forward to a safer and more seamless riding experience, with fewer interruptions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: With these developments, more journeys can be carried out entirely on the cycling path network, as Mr Yee Chia Hsing has pointed out.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: Lastly, we need to develop the right culture of graciousness.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: This is critical in densely populated Singapore, where users of different modes of transport are constantly in close proximity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: The Active Mobility Advisory Panel (AMAP) will continue to promote greater acceptance of active mobility in Singapore by focusing more on engagement and educational measures, and calling on all path users to be safe and considerate.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: Going forward, how can we do better, together?

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: On roads, motorists should practice good road safety habits and be vigilant and look out for other road users.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: On paths, device users should watch out for other path users and ride safely and considerately.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: Pedestrians should also be alert to their surroundings and keep to the left unless overtaking.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: They should walk on footpaths wherever they are, located adjacent to cycling paths.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: We will also continue to monitor the environmental impact of our other land transport projects.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: We have engaged stakeholders extensively since 2013 and will continue to do so even as the project enters the Advanced Engineering Studies phase.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Lam Pin Min)
text: I will now hand over to Senior Minister of State Janil Puthucheary, who will explain our strategies for a sustainable land transport system.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Mr Chairman, several Members have asked questions or provided suggestions that I will address in my response.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Mr Ang Wei Neng, Ms Sun Xueling, Mr Melvin Yong and Miss Cheng Li Hui have brought up issues such as COVID-19, taxi and private hire car (PHC) drivers, the transition to the Bus Contracting Model, the push for electric vehicles and the necessary incentives and infrastructure.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: They have also asked about our plans for autonomous vehicles and the future professional development of our transport workforce.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: COVID-19 has affected the public transport and point-to-point sectors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The taxi and PHC drivers' livelihoods have been badly affected.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: They need help so that they can continue to provide sustainable services for Singaporean commuters.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Drivers who do not meet the eligibility criteria can seek help via the Government-NTUC Driver Care Fund.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We hope that this will help the drivers through this difficult period.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: But COVID-19 could have a longer term impact, so we are working closely with the operators and the driver associations to monitor the situation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Even as we deal with COVID-19's immediate impact, we must push on with our plans for a future-ready land transport system.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The Land Transport Masterplan 2040 (LTMP 2040) sets out this long-term vision that we have for our land transport system.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: It was developed in consultation with over 7,000 Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: And many participants recognised that Singapore is running up against tighter land, manpower, fiscal and environmental constraints.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Long-term sustainability has to be a key planning consideration for our transport system.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: There are three critical strategies for us to achieve this long-term sustainability of our land transport system.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: First, we have to make Walk-Cycle-Ride (WCR) the preferred modes of transport here in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Walking – connecting us to the transport nodes, to the MRT, to the buses, and also to the amenities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Cycling – for those who can, as a very efficient and healthy way of getting around town.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: And riding – whether it is the MRT, the bus or shared vehicles, in preference to private car ownership.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The second key strategy is to move comprehensively to cleaner and greener vehicles – dealing with the emissions, dealing with resource utilisation and the issues around carbon.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Thirdly, we have to optimise our land transport system for the future.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Every little bit of marginal gain – whether it is safety, whether it is efficiency, whether it is cost, whether it is the experience of the commuters – is important; and the best way to do so is to appropriately and correctly use technology to optimise our land transport system.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: First strategy on making Walk-Cycle-Ride the preferred modes of transport.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: It is sustainable, and Minister Khaw spoke about our ambitions for a world-class public transport network, our investments over the next decade to renew and expand the rail network.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Senior Minister of State Dr Lam Pin Min spoke about how cycling and active mobility can play an appropriate role in this landscape.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Today, they already connect millions of Singaporeans to their homes, their schools and their offices on a daily basis.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The Public Transport Council's annual Public Transport Customer Satisfaction Survey (PTCSS) shows that commuter satisfaction in our public bus services continues to be high.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The Bus Contracting Model (BCM) played an important part in achieving this.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We have injected additional capacity through the BCM for more than 100 bus services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We have also built, replaced or upgraded 16 bus interchanges island-wide to keep pace with this larger bus fleet.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Peak-hour bus waiting times for trunk services have come down from 20 minutes or less in 2016 to 15 minutes or less today.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: These improvements would not have been possible without the hard work, the dedication and the commitment of our bus captains.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The BCM was a major change for our bus industry and tripartite partners worked closely together to ensure a smooth transition.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: In particular, the National Transport Workers' Union (NTWU) played a key role in the development of tripartite guidelines to protect the welfare of bus sector employees and our bus captains.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Bus operators competing for contracts under the BCM have to abide by these guidelines, which ensure that bus employees will be treated fairly and will be no worse off when a new operator takes on a contract.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Through this close partnership with NTWU, we have seen improvements to the working conditions for bus captains, such as upgraded staff canteens and more rest areas.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The starting monthly pay for new local bus captains has also increased by over 25% since 2014, higher than the national wage growth of 18% over the same period.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: All of these would not have been possible without the NTWU's leadership and active participation, and we very much appreciate their contribution to this effort.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Our second strategy – to encourage cleaner and greener vehicles.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: It appears self-evident and has been discussed at great length in other parts of this Committee of Supply (COS) and also in the debate on the Budget.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: It is important and it is vital as we continue to grow our land transport system.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Today, we have close to 900,000 ICE vehicles, and this will require an extensive transformation of the fleet, significant changes in commuting and consumer behaviour, and development of the necessary supporting infrastructure to achieve this vision.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Today, Electric Vehicles (EVs) are the most promising cleaner vehicle technology.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Car manufacturers are developing new models that are energy efficient and increasingly cost effective.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Other technologies such as the hydrogen fuel cell vehicles, could be viable in the future, but today they are currently less suited for mainstream use.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We in Singapore lack a supply of green hydrogen to power hydrogen fuel cell vehicles.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: So, if we choose that path there will be a higher cost associated with the technology, infrastructure and refuelling.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Nevertheless, we will continue to monitor developments and we will move in a way towards this vision for 2040 that will allow us to adapt to other technologies in the future.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: It is an ambitious undertaking and there are serious challenges that we will need to overcome.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The Government will make four moves to achieve this vision.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: First, we will ensure that there is enough charging infrastructure accessible to EV owners.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: It will not be easy, but this is very important.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Because if you are considering purchasing an EV over an ICE vehicle, you have to be convinced that you have access to a charger which is as convenient as access to a petrol station.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: As a first step, we will prioritise the charging provision at carparks, starting with public carparks.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We will also work with the private sector to improve charging provisions at private carparks.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We encourage charging providers to partner private developers and building owners, as many of them are keen to increase the availability of EV charging on their premises.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Greater EV adoption will result in an increase in electricity demand and we will be able to manage this because we will build new power generation capacity and we will reinforce our grid network.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We will also incorporate innovations such as smart charging and energy storage solutions that store energy from the grid during off-peak periods.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We are conducting studies to better understand the different factors that affect the demand for charging and we will also study potential solutions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This will guide our planned roll-out of the infrastructure needed.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The second move that we will make is to incentivise demand for EVs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: It is a large cost gap for a prospective EV owner.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: EV sales accounted for less than 0.1% of all new private car sales over the last five years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This is why Deputy Prime Minister announced the EV Early Adoption Incentive at Budget this year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: With further adoption and new models, this cost gap will close further.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We expect EVs to reach cost parity with ICE vehicles by the mid 2020s.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: In the meantime, we hope that this incentive will serve as an early signal to encourage more prospective car owners to consider EVs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We also hope that car dealers will be encouraged to bring in more EV models.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This will provide more choice for consumers and cater to the increase in demand.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Mass market EV taxi models will only need to pay the minimum Additional Registration Fee of $5,000.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: As fleets like taxis stand to benefit more from the lower per mile cost of EVs, we hope this incentivises more taxi companies to expand their electric taxi fleet.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Although existing EV owners are not eligible for the EV Early Adoption Incentive, they will benefit from the technical revision to the variable component of their road tax from 1 January 2021 onwards.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: As a special transitional arrangement, we will exempt them from the additional flat component of the new EV road tax that was introduced at this year’s Budget.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This component was introduced to partly account for the loss in fuel excise duties that EVs do not incur.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: It will be waived for a three-year period from 1 January 2021 to 31 December 2023 for all EVs registered before this period.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: So, in future, going forward there will be an incentive for new purchasers of EVs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: And owners of existing EVs, prior to 1 January 2021, will all see a reduction in road tax during this period.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The third move is that the Government will take the lead to green our fleets.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Since last March, we have deployed 50 diesel hybrid buses on the roads.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We have also bought 60 fully electric buses and will be deploying them progressively this year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: New bus depots will be designed to support electric buses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: As we gradually replace our existing diesel buses with cleaner energy ones, Singaporeans will enjoy quieter commutes and cleaner air.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The fourth move is that we will update our regulations to keep pace with technology.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This is in addition to the low-powered e-motorcycles which are already allowed today, and will add to the cleaner vehicle options available.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This means that public charging points in Singapore can include these CHAdeMO chargers from today onwards.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Prospective car owners will then be able to choose from a wider range of EV models, including those that use these CHAdeMO chargers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We will continue to review and refresh our regulations on EVs to ensure that these keep pace with industry developments.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: To recap, four moves to drive the strategy of EV adoption in Singapore: build up charging infrastructure, incentivise the purchase of EV vehicles, Government will take the lead with our fleet and updating our regulations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: For our third strategy – harnessing technology to optimise land transport for the future.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We have always relied on new technology to improve our transport system and deliver better transport outcomes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: There are examples such as how today, you can plan your journey by looking up bus arrival times through the MyTransport app.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Commuters can sign up for SimplyGo, allowing you to pay for public transport using your contactless bank card, so you no longer have to top-up your stored value cards.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: A further use of technology is Autonomous Vehicles (AVs).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: These have the potential to improve connectivity by more efficiently offering dynamically-routed forms of shared transport.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Our AV trials have come a long way since one-north was designated as the first site for AV public road testing in 2015.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: These trials have allowed developers to enhance their technology through real-world applications, and helped LTA learn how to safely introduce AVs to improve our transport network.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The trials have also created opportunities for the public to interact with AV technology.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Around 6,000 visitors tried out the on-demand driverless shuttles in Sentosa last year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The feedback was positive, with most visitors indicating that they enjoyed the ride, mostly because for them it is really no different from a usual bus ride.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We aim to progress to the next stage of trials with pilot deployment in the early 2020s.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We have launched a Call-For-Collaboration last year and there has been keen interest from more than 20 companies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We are currently assessing and looking through their proposals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Safety and public acceptance will continue to be top priorities as we progress to pilot the deployment in other areas.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: But even as we continue to study and adopt new technologies, we have to ensure that this benefits our people through better jobs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: AVs will transform the transport sector and create new jobs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Today, some of our public transport operators have already taken steps to familiarise our bus captains with AV bus operations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: So, these bus captains then become confident of working with AV technologies in the future.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This will identify emerging skills and new job roles arising from AV deployment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: On-the-job training and courses on AV safety protocol and operations will also be developed.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We plan to train about 100 bus captains as a start.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: These efforts are part of the Land Transport Industry Transformation Map 2.0.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The Government will continue to work closely with the unions and industry to prepare our workers for new job opportunities in the sector.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Another initiative borne out of this close tripartite relationship is the Rail Manpower Development Package (RMDP).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The RMDP aims to expand the rail workforce and accelerate workforce transformation over the next five years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: RMDP will also attract, retain and raise the profile of rail professionals through the launch of new SGRail Industry Scholarships and Sponsorships.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: These will be open to fresh graduates and in-service staff to pursue further studies at Institutes of Higher Learning.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: By investing in our rail workers, we are also investing in the future of rail reliability.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Beyond bus and rail workers, we will also continue to provide retraining and upskilling opportunities for taxi and PHC drivers, including allowing them to move laterally into adjacent sectors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The taxi and PHC operators have worked closely with the driver associations, with support from SkillsFuture Singapore, to develop training programmes for the drivers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We will continue to work with operators and unions to equip our land transport workforce with the necessary skills and capabilities for the next phase of development.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: There is a lot of work ahead of us to achieve all of this.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We invite Singaporeans to partner us on this journey.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Together, we can build a sustainable land transport system that brings Singapore together, one which future generations of Singaporeans will enjoy and feel proud of.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Mr Chairman, the COVID-19 situation over the past weeks has reminded us of the importance of safety and inclusivity in Singapore’s transport system.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: During this difficult period, it is even more important that we ensure that no one is left behind, especially the elderly and vulnerable.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: In fact, safety and inclusivity have been priorities for transport, way before COVID-19 outbreak.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: In 2018, we announced plans to implement the Red-Amber-Green (RAG) arrows at all feasible traffic junctions to replace discretionary right turns and improve pedestrian safety.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We continue to strive towards a "Vision Zero" environment with fewer land transport-related fatalities, through regulations at the vehicle, driver and operator levels.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Not only will this give confidence to commuters, this is also for the drivers' own safety.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Mr Muhamad Faisal Manap asked about streamlining the medical examinations for elderly taxi drivers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: On the statutory age limit, we need to bear in mind that taxi driving is physically and mentally demanding, and can have serious impact on commuters and other road users.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This move will bring greater convenience to our elderly taxi drivers.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: It is important to ensure that vocation drivers are fit to drive as they perform a public service.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: However, we are aware that with improve healthcare, drivers may be able to drive longer.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We are studying the possibility of raising the statutory age limits of our elderly vocation drivers together with the Singapore Medical Association.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Mr Png Eng Huat also asked about Pedestrian Overhead Bridges (POBs).

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Indeed, our preference is to build crossings at-grade, rather than POBs, as they are all barrier-free and can be more easily accessed by the elderly and people with mobility challenges.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: However, there are instances where such at-grade crossings are dangerous, for example across major roads with fast-moving traffic, or when they may cause serious traffic congestion.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Even then, we will do our best to meet the needs of our elderly and the less ambulant.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We plan to install lifts at all new POBs near major transport hubs and other existing POBs, if possible.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: As these lifts are costly, priority is given to the POBs which will most benefit the less mobile.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Since March 2015, we have gradually introduced priority queues at transport nodes, so that individuals with special needs can board buses and trains more easily.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Building on this effort, we will also start trialling the use of priority cabins on the North East Line trains towards the end of this year.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Commuters in these cabins, which will be located near station lifts where possible, are encouraged to give way to the more vulnerable commuters, such as the elderly, wheelchair users and families with young children.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The idea for this initiative came from the various public engagements done to better understand commuters' needs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: As Singaporeans' mobility needs change, our transport system also needs to keep pace.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Where suitable, the Government will continue to make our transport system even safer and more inclusive.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: To enhance road safety for senior pedestrians, we have introduced 17 Silver Zones since 2014 with 18 currently in progress.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: These zones have narrower roads, speed humps to reduce traffic speed and two-stage crossings for senior pedestrians to pause and rest, making road crossing safer for them.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We are also constantly looking to improve upon existing results, for example, we will be trying lower speed limits at specific Silver Zones in the coming months to enhance road safety for our senior pedestrians.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: To help the visually impaired navigate through our transport system, we piloted the mobile application, Mobility Assistance for the Visually Impaired and Selected Users (MAVIS).

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The app was piloted on selected buses since January 2019.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: MAVIS alerts bus drivers when commuters with special needs are boarding and alighting and allows visually impaired commuters to activate an audio announcement at the boarding bus-stop to guide them to their arriving bus.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This might not mean a lot to able-bodied commuters, but to the visually impaired, these functions help them get around more conveniently and safely.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We have received heart-felt feedback from commuters on how MAVIS had made a difference in their lives, giving them more confidence to take the bus, especially when there is no one around to help.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Members would have also read about LTA's upcoming hands-free ticketing trial, which supports our effort to make it even more convenient for commuters with special needs to travel on our buses and trains, without the need to tap their fare cards.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Mr Chairman, the Government's efforts alone are not enough to make our land transport system safe and inclusive.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: For example, even if we build more lifts at existing train stations, it will not help vulnerable commuters if others compete to use the lifts.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We will continue to encourage individual commuters to be more understanding about those with different needs from ours, be more gracious in putting others' needs before ours, and even better, be more caring by going the extra mile for fellow commuters, especially the elderly and those with special needs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Mr Lester Wong was on the train when an elderly woman fell with her groceries and could not get up.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Lester went out of his way to accompany her home, to make sure that the elderly was alright.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Upon reaching home and taking a rest, the elderly was still not feeling well, so Lester insisted on sending her to the hospital to make sure that she got the medical care and attention she needed.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Lester was the winner of the first Caring Commuter award last year.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Over the past years, we have heard many stories like Lester's and there are probably many more that we do not know of.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: It is not always easy to know what kind of help others need, or if and when we should even offer help.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This is why one of the Committee's first goals is to help commuters better understand other commuters' needs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We will encourage commuters who need help to ask for help too, so that it is easier for their fellow commuters to step up and provide the necessary care.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Over the next six months, the Committee will organise two series of engagements.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: To begin, we will engage widely to gather ideas and views on how we, as commuters, can contribute to this cause.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Then, we will engage commuters in targeted ways to pilot and co-create solutions that can help to grow the movement.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Mr Chairman, the industry will also need to lean forward to play their part in making our land transport system safer and more inclusive for all Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: There may be some initiatives that are difficult for the Government to mandate and implement alone.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: An example would be the provision of child seats in taxis.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This was discussed extensively during our public consultations for the P2P regulatory review and had mixed views from drivers, operators and the public.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This will enhance safety for children in taxis and provide parents of young children with a safer transport option.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Over the past weeks, we have seen even more instances of the industry stepping up to partner the Government, coming together during these difficult times.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: This had helped to provide peace of mind for the frontliners of our battle against COVID-19, to know that they can have a much needed, more comfortable ride home after a stressful day at work caring for fellow Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: While COVID-19 would eventually run its course, the partnerships forged during this difficult time cannot end.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We will continue to strengthen these ties and forge new partnerships as we build a transport system that is safer and more inclusive for all Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Such partnerships are pivotal in the next phase of Singapore's development.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: The Government cannot and should not do this alone.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: We will need to tap on synergies across sectors and harness the strength of our entire community.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: As a whole, we are greater than the sum of our individual parts.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng)
text: Working closely together with commuters, the industry and the community, we will achieve our vision of a safe and inclusive transport system for all.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee
text: Chairman, I have a clarification for the Senior Minister of State Lam.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee
text: Beyond monitoring the take-up rate of training for aviation crew.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee
text: I know that the Senior Minister of State takes a personal interest in many transport workers.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee
text: Hopefully, the class can start within the month so that we can get a sense of whether the $112 million support to the aviation sector is reaching the workers and what has the workers' response been.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee
text: We have a Skills Framework and the Industry Transformation Map.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee
text: So, delivering training to the workers should be something that the training bodies and the various partners can deliver.

speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee
text: And I would like to invite the Senior Minister of State to do that visit soon.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: And I understand that he is equally concerned about the welfare of the workers.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: As I am aware, it is already quite well-received on the ground.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: But rest assured, I will be happy to accept the invitation by Mr Ang Hin Kee to visit them once you are ready.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: Chairman, I thank Minister Khaw, Senior Minister of State Lam and Senior Minister of State Janil for answering some of the questions I have raised.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: I have a clarification for Senior Minister of State Janil.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: In my Budget debate speech, I raised the issue of the Government's handling of the foreign internal combustion engine (ICE) vehicles issue in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: I am saying this because I think we all know that there are plenty of Malaysian lorries, buses motorcycles and passenger vehicles that come in and out of Singapore almost on a daily basis.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: I am sure that the Government would have to factor the presence of this large number of foreign ICE vehicles in Singapore as we work towards the plan in 2040.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: So, I will be grateful for the clarification.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Mr Chairman, I thank the Member Mr Dennis Tan for his question.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Certainly, the presence of foreign ICE vehicles is going to be an important consideration going forward.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We are just getting started on our journey.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: If you look at what we are doing with the incentives, the waiver of some of the tax structures and some of the changes that we have to make, our regulatory space has not quite settled.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: But when it does and as it does, one of the things we will have to look at is the relationship between what we do for Singaporean vehicles and then how that impacts what happens to non-Singaporean vehicles that are ICE vehicles when they come in.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, it is a factor but a it is a little bit premature to be absolutely settled on how it should be treated at this point.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
text: I know there are trials on AVs in NUS and NTU.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
text: But can he elaborate more because the public wants to be absolutely sure that AVs are safe on the road.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Mr Chairman, I thank Mr Sitoh for the question and I am going to answer the question even though he directed it to my colleague, Mr Baey Yam Keng.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Absolutely, public safety is a key consideration in how we develop our AVs.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: It is part of our phased and gated approach in the AV development.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: But it is also part of how we hope to have opportunities for the public to experience Autonomous Vehicles in a safe and controlled manner; and for the developers and operators to then learn about what is the public experience on Autonomous Vehicles so that the experience can be improved.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: I follow-up on that question on autonomous vehicles, beyond safety, I am asking about job security.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: Autonomous Vehicles can potentially disrupt the livelihood of more than 50,000 workers who depend on driving to make a living.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: I am heartened to hear the efforts are already being made to familiarise our Bus Captains with AV technology.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: The union has been working very closely with LTA on that.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: But there are others such as taxi drivers, private hire drivers, heavy vehicle drivers, school bus drivers, and recently, I even visited and found that even driving instructors will be impacted and eventually displaced by AV technology.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: We must not forget them in our push towards AVs.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Mr Chairman, absolutely, we would be very happy to work with NTUC and our tripartite partners.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: I think it is essential that we do so and we would not be able to address the space adequately if it were not for the strong partnerships that we are able to develop.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: I would assure Mr Melvin Yong and his union colleagues that there will be plenty of jobs.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The one thing we cannot be assured of is that everything will stay the same.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: But there will be plenty of jobs and if we take the right approach in terms of thinking ahead, developing these roadmaps around retraining and re-skilling, and then having our workers and our unions actively engage in that process of retraining and re-skilling, then everybody will be well looked after.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: I have two clarifications on the Cross Island Line (CRL).

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: But can I check whether we are looking into moving just a partial worksite of A1W1, or moving the entire worksite into the non-playing areas in SICC?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: The second question is with regard to the establishment of the Environmental Advisory Panel that we are setting up to provide independent assessment of the implementation of the environmental monitoring and management plan.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Can I just check who is LTA going to select to be part of this Panel?

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Before I dwell into the questions that he has asked, I would like to assure the House that LTA, as well as MOT, have been working very, very closely with the nature groups in this journey.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We have been engaging the nature groups and various stakeholders very intensively over the past six to seven years.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: I myself have met the nature groups' leadership on many occasions; even my predecessor, Minister Josephine Teo had done the same.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: And this trust that we have built between MOT, LTA and the nature groups (NGs), is a very strong one.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Therefore, I would like to reassure Mr Louis Ng as well as the rest of the nature groups' leadership, that we continue to work with them, even after the announcement of the alignment of CRL.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We shall wait for the report of the study before we can ascertain exactly how much we can optimise A1W1.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: But rest assured that we are also in a discussion with SICC to see how we can use some of the non-play sites within the golf course, so that we can minimise the impact of the the engineering works to the environment.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: I understand that Mr Louis Ng is also quite concerned about the Raffles Banded Langurs.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: There has been actually quite a number of mitigating measures suggested by Dr Andie Ang and we are currently working very closely with her.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: With respect to the Member's specific question on the worksite, like I have mentioned, we will await the study, but definitely we will see how we can optimise the site in order to minimise the impact on the primates that he has mentioned – Leonardo, Michelangelo, Donatello and Raphael.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: We will make sure that the impact will be kept to a minimal, as much as possible.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: As to the Member's second question on the Advisory Panel, I think we shall wait for LTA to make the necessary announcement.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: The first question pertains to a point I raised in my Budget debate speech about private bus drivers in Singapore and some of their concerns arising out of the COVID-19 situation.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: Does MOT have a perspective or position on how they can be helped and reached out to, in this time of need?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: The second clarification arises from Senior Minister of State Janil's sharing on the purchase of public buses.

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: What initiatives does the Ministry have in mind for the earlier adaptation for electric buses for the private sector?

speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
text: There are a lot of buses that are used to transport workers in Singapore, for example, and that can only support the Government's mission of the transit to electric vehicles in general.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The best help for the private bus drivers is going to be when business is usual is returned to and the tourists come back and workers need to be transferred and the current crisis is over.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: They will benefit from some of the measures that are in the larger support package for businesses in general and for Singaporeans in general.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We have not gotten a specific package for private bus drivers, but as business entities in general, they will be assisted.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: But it is something we were looking at.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: And if there is an appropriate way and appropriate opportunity to do so, it is something that we can consider.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: There are differences though, through the taxi operators, for example.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: There are ways in which we make sure that it goes down to the individual worker and so forth, and that is, the outcome that we would like to achieve.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The difficulty, of course, is that there are not quite as many models and platforms of that size today.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: There will be, as the technology improves, but we hope to be able to incentivise this from the emissions perspective.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The 60 buses that Mr Singh mentioned – 50 diesel hybrid – they demonstrate some of the difficulties that we have.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We are exploring how to deploy and operationalise this technology and see what we need in terms of maintenance or depot reconfiguration, changes to the skill sets in our workers.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: And that is something where we have the entire network to deal with.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: I think for the smaller operators, it may take a little bit longer before they are able to make these changes.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing
text: How do we move from 0.1% to 100% in 10 years?

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing
text: The other feedback is that there are a lot of car models, EV models which are available in the UK, but the dealers do not bring them in.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing
text: What is MOT doing to push all these dealers to bring these models in?

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing
text: That is one feedback from consumers, that they have very limited EV choices.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Over the lifetime of a vehicle, an electric vehicle, hopefully, should incur less maintenance cost, the mechanisms are easier to maintain, and also less energy cost.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, the short answer is we hope consumers will make the choice and we are trying to incentivise consumers to make the choice, as a result of which dealers should respond.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Internationally, many manufacturers are developing new models and have committed in some cases, to only develop electric models past a certain date.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: That should also help to lower the price of these vehicles.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: Put together, we hope that over the next 10 years, there are increasing reasons for Singaporeans who choose to buy a car to choose to buy an electric car.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: And then, we hope that somewhere around 2030, we will have the last sale of an internal combustion engine vehicle and then, over a 10-year cycle by 2040, we will have an entire cleaner and greener fleet here in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
text: Mr Chairman, I thank all Members for their speeches and contributions.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
text: In particular, I would like to thank the MOT team for their hard work and support.
